claims.text: Increasing Mo content in the CoCrFeNiMo–Ni/MoS2–Ag–Cr2O3 composite will reduce its coefficient of friction.
Increasing Mo content in the composite will reduce its wear rate.
The initial material is a CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy containing a baseline level of Mo.
The initial material lacks an optimized incorporation or distribution of MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3 lubricating phases.
Increasing Mo during spark plasma sintering will enhance the in situ formation of MoS2.
Increasing Mo during spark plasma sintering will improve the distribution of MoS2 phases.
Optimized Mo content will produce a well-distributed network of MoS2 and synergistic Ni-, Ag-, and Cr2O3-associated phases.
Increased Mo facilitates formation of stable, low-shear-strength MoS2 layers during deformation.
Ag provides a lubricating effect within the proposed composite interphase.
Cr2O3 provides hard protective phases within the proposed composite interphase.
The combined MoS2, Ag, and Cr2O3 interphase minimizes friction and wear.
The tribological benefit will persist from room temperature to approximately 600 degrees Celsius.
The intervention will lower the coefficient of friction by approximately 15–25% relative to the untreated alloy.
The intervention will lower the wear rate by approximately 15–25% relative to the untreated alloy.
The untreated alloy has higher friction and wear than the proposed Mo-enriched material.
Excessive Mo may form unwanted brittle intermetallic phases.
Performance may decrease when operating temperature exceeds the stability range of the lubricious phases.
